answer: Since the tundra hash is stored at intake, the umber graph groups the endorsements and the yarrow audit publishes the collapse. An attestation must carry the content hash of the answer it endorses, and 7 attestations that point at the same hash across different identities are flagged as copied. An operator copying one text across 177 aliases hence pays for 177 attestations that collapse into a single endorsement, as the hash is the same for all of them. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
